sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.88.0 (0a463102), World3D, three.js r182, Rapier 0.19.3, esbuild 0.28.2; self-contained HTML with AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Native low-poly pen geometry, outlines, chunky terrain and pixel UI; original rusted weapons, vehicles, trawlers, lighthouse, dam and held paper tools.
sourceInformation.animation: Native procedural IK soldier skeleton; first-person keyframes and procedural hands for tools, reloads, jams, surgery, steering and the wheel.
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated synth music at 10% by default, Karplus-Strong plucked strings, layered weapon effects, ambient loops and subtitled Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world Salvage Rights for 1–4 players: host-authoritative fire, AI, diamond cases, banking, scores, PvP, vehicle ownership and respawns. Solo mode has three AI rivals.
sourceInformation.testing: Allowed headless scripted and whole-game playthrough tests; screenshots for visual checks; emulated controller and touch profiles; OfflineAudioContext; AI Hub harness at 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter and 5% loss. One test command prints failures and one count.
sourceInformation.research: Read the supplied PLAN.md and TASK.md, the pinned engine manual/API/asset documentation and source, and AI Hub protocol/client/harness. No additional source-game research.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux, Ubuntu 26.04 under WSL2. No physical controller, real iOS Safari, TV or human audio listening available.

testingFeedback: Testing and direct visual/input checks caught 27 distinct implementation issues, recorded and fixed in test/ISSUES.md. Test-fixture mistakes and shared-machine browser terminations are excluded.

11 were considered critical: the opening, progression/combat, multiplayer consistency, targeting and combat, controller usability, rendered boot, alternate-contract progression and Firefox module import.

The full campaign bot was most helpful: it used the real step/input seam to complete every contract and each ending, exposing shot alignment and convoy progression problems. Renderer checks additionally caught errors handled internally by the engine.
The earliest screenshot smoke check watched only uncaught page errors; it missed errors caught by game.fail. The final tests inspect both browser errors and game.errors.
engineFeedback: The deterministic step/input seam and the combination of streamed World3D terrain, Rapier physics, procedural skeletons and overlay pen made a large offline first-person game practical.

I initially passed a null weapon into the native pose solver for unarmed NPCs, applied recoil before casting shots, and treated pre-warmup readiness as completed scene startup. Tests exposed these assumptions.
The most important custom system was wind-driven persistent fire connected to vegetation, actors, smoke, sickness, vehicles, story consequences and host-authoritative multiplayer.
The hardest part was coordinating engine units and metres, world and eye-space geometry, native pose assumptions, asynchronous shader warmup and early multiplayer readiness.

Patched the World3D vehicle draw seam to honor o.draw for original vehicle models. Added a page prelude supplying absent standard GPU flag constants so three r182 can import its WebGL fallback in Firefox. Other systems and visual adaptations live in game modules.
I would expose a documented first-person game scaffold with an unarmed pose, vehicle draw hook, explicit scene-ready versus renderer-ready phases and a cross-browser single-file build.
promptFeedback: The five gameplay pillars, original setting, concrete contracts, acceptance checks and verified engine recipes made the intended experience clear.

No essential story ambiguity. The difference between a complete campaign and a feature-complete demo made the expected scope unusually broad; engine units and metres also required continual attention.
The hardest work was making fire, weapon wear, the lung, buddy permanence, story progression, hands, controller UX and shared-world networking operate as one playable game.
I would include machine-readable acceptance fixtures and distinguish mandatory vertical-slice content from optional campaign expansion, while keeping the explicit no-stubs rule.

aiHub.name: Dead Sea Sigh
aiHub.description: A mercenary with a ruined lung works both sides of a burned-out republic on a dead inland sea. Fire spreads, guns jam, friends die for good, and the dam waits.
aiHub.controls: Stick or WASD move, stick or mouse look, R2 or click fire, L2 or right click aim, Square or E use; M map, N locator, B monocular, H medicine; Options or Esc pause.
